view_frame: The drawing presents a TOP view in the XY plane and an END SECTION view. The world frame is defined with X as width (horizontal in TOP view), Y as depth (vertical in TOP view), and Z as height (vertical in END SECTION view). The part lies flat in the XY plane with its section height along Z.

features.placement: The path consists of two straight segments and one 180-degree arc. The arc centre is at (0, 15). The arc spans from angle 180 degrees to 0 degrees (clockwise traversal relative to the centre, or counter-clockwise from 180 to 360/0). The left straight segment runs from (-20, 15) to (-20, 0). The right straight segment runs from (20, 15) to (20, 0). The section is a 6mm (width) x 8mm (height) rectangle. The section centre is lifted to Z=4 (half of 8mm) to sit on the bed.
features.evidence: TOP view shows a U-shaped path. Text specifies '180° bend', 'Centreline radius R20', 'Both straight ends: 15 long', 'Same 6 x 8 section throughout'. END SECTION shows a rectangle 6 wide and 8 high. 'Section remains upright along Z'.

connections: The left straight segment connects tangentially to the left end of the 180-degree arc.
The right straight segment connects tangentially to the right end of the 180-degree arc.
edit_rules: Changing the section width (6) or height (8) updates the sweep profile but maintains the centreline path.
Changing the centreline radius (R20) moves the arc endpoints and the start of the straight segments.
Changing the straight length (15) moves the free ends of the straight segments along Y.
The overall width (46) is derived from 2 * (Centreline Radius + Section Width / 2) = 2 * (20 + 3) = 46. If Centreline Radius or Section Width changes, Overall Width must be recalculated.
